title: Move Semantics and Value Categories
learningObjectives: Explain the main ideas of Move Semantics and Value Categories.
Identify the language rules and relevant C++ constructs.
Apply the topic in a small program.
Recognize common pitfalls and safety concerns.
Test an example and justify design decisions.

understand.concept: Move semantics can transfer resources instead of copying. std::move is a cast enabling move overload selection, not the transfer itself. Moved-from objects remain valid but generally unspecified.
understand.whyItMatters: Moving can reduce expensive copies for resource-owning types, but source-state assumptions cause bugs.
understand.explain: Use std::move when transfer is intended, then don't rely on moved-from content. Standard containers remain valid after moves.
